channel.title: Columbia Journalism Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Columbia Journalism Review (cjr.org)

item.title: The Drug War in Full View
item.description: A profile of El Mencho. Plus: An incredibly long State of the Union that no one will remember; history repeats, nastily, in Georgia.

item.title: A Cauldron of Ideas to Fight Misinformation
item.description: A new app combines peer-reviewed posts, crypto micropayments, AI, and blockchain technology to verify what’s going on in Ukraine.

item.title: Blackout Iran
item.description: When the Trump administration launched a major attack on Iran, news organizations had to navigate a shaky environment for communications—and moral clarity.

item.title: Capitol Newbies
item.description: The University of Missouri students bringing regional reporting back to Washington.

item.title: ‘Of Course Iranians Want Change. The Question Is, What Kind of Change?’
item.description: As bombs rain down, Babak Rahimi, a scholar of the Middle East, challenges the US press to convey the “messy” reality on the ground.

item.title: The New York Times Takes the Pentagon to Court
item.description: As the US wages war on Iran, journalists’ fight for access enters a new phase.

item.title: Hyperlocal AI with a Million Subscribers
item.description: Patch built a newsletter system to be not hard-nosed journalism but a community-building tool.

item.title: To Survive the AI Age, Publishers Are Finally Working Together
item.description: UK publishers are banding together to create standards for responsible AI—amid Anthropic’s stark reminders of its potential for harm.

item.title: Iranian Journalists Behind Bars
item.description: Devastation in Iran. Plus: The death of a refugee in Buffalo, and the military’s “simmering white Christian nationalism.”

item.title: A Reporter in Nashville, Detained by ICE
item.description: Estefany Rodríguez, a journalist for a Spanish-language outlet, was covering immigration raids. The next day, agents arrested her without a warrant.
